one_liner: Baseline-JPEG decoder for microcontrollers and PCs; decoded 1.7x faster than TJpgDec and 3.4x faster than picojpeg on an ESP32-S3.
what_it_does: Decodes baseline Huffman JPEGs (grayscale or YCbCr, 4:4:4, 4:2:2 either orientation, 4:2:0) from RAM, flash or caller-supplied file callbacks, and hands pixels to a draw callback in blocks of up to 2048 pixels (RGB565 little or big endian, RGB8888, 8-bit gray, or 1/2/4-bpp Floyd-Steinberg dithered) or writes them into a caller framebuffer. The API is a C++ class (openRAM/openFLASH/open, then decode(x, y, options) with 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 scaling, crop, Exif-thumbnail and DMA ping-pong flags) plus an equivalent C API (JPEG_openRAM, JPEG_decode, ...). It is not a drop-in for the libjpeg API or for TJpgDec; progressive files are decoded only as 1/8-scale DC thumbnails.
how_it_is_fast: Table-driven Huffman decoding: DC codes go through a 6-bit short table plus a long table for codes starting with five 1 bits (short codes have the magnitude bits folded into the entry), AC codes through a 10-bit short table plus a long table for codes starting with six 1 bits, read from a 32- or 64-bit bit buffer refilled with byte-swapped word loads; FF00 byte-stuffing is removed in bulk ahead of decode (SSE2/NEON in JPEGFilter). The integer AAN-style IDCT tracks which columns and rows hold non-zero coefficients and skips the empty ones, DC-only blocks are filled directly, 1/4 and 1/8 scaling use 2x2 and DC-only transforms, and MCUs outside a crop rectangle decode only their DC term. SIMD IDCT and colour conversion exist for x86-64 SSE2 and AArch64 NEON; on the ESP32-S3, hand-written assembly (s3_simd_420.S, s3_simd_444.S, s3_simd_dequant.S) does YCbCr-to-RGB565 conversion and dequantisation with the S3's 128-bit vector instructions (an S3 IDCT file is still marked _FUTURE).
when_to_use: Showing baseline JPEGs on an MCU-driven LCD (ESP32, ESP32-S3, Cortex-M4/M7, Teensy and similar) where about 18-20 KB of RAM for the decoder is affordable and lower latency than TJpgDec or picojpeg matters.
MJPEG or camera-frame playback on an ESP32-S3 at small resolutions: atomic14 measured about 23-32 ms for a 280x240 frame, and pixels can be streamed to SPI DMA while the next MCU row decodes.
Images larger than the screen: built-in 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 scaling, cropping and Exif-thumbnail extraction avoid decoding pixels you will throw away.
E-paper or monochrome displays: the 1/2/4-bpp dithered output path saves a separate dithering pass.

Small dependency-free baseline decoding on a host (Linux, macOS, Windows x64) when one translation unit with SSE2/NEON is enough and decode speed versus libjpeg-turbo is not the deciding factor (no such comparison has been published).
when_not_to_use: Progressive JPEGs at full size: only a 1/8-scale DC thumbnail is produced. Use libjpeg-turbo on hosts, or lowzag for scaled progressive decoding on an ESP32.
Untrusted input on MCUs without memory protection: an out-of-bounds write in the progressive decoder is open (issue #119) and there is no fuzzing or hardening record in the repository.
Desktop throughput work: there is no measurement against libjpeg-turbo, and arithmetic coding, 12-bit and lossless JPEG are not listed as supported.
RAM-starved MCUs: each JPEGDEC object embeds about 17.9 KB of state, while TJpgDec runs in a 3.1-3.5 KB workspace.

ESP32-S3 boards with PSRAM where the whole frame can be buffered: Espressif's ESP32_JPEG decoded the same image faster (20 ms vs 23 ms), at the cost of a full output buffer and a precompiled binary library.

integration.form: source-drop / Arduino library (src/JPEGDEC.cpp includes src/jpeg.inl, plus three ESP32-S3 .S files); ESP-IDF component; linux/makefile builds a static library
integration.dependencies: none for the decoder core; Arduino.h on Arduino builds; library.properties lists bb_spi_lcd (for the JPEGDisplay helper); the ESP-IDF CMakeLists.txt REQUIRES esp-dsp and arduino-esp32; the S3 SIMD path is compiled only when esp-dsp's dsps_fft2r_platform.h is found
integration.min_toolchain: C++ class without exceptions or STL; uses GCC/Clang builtins (__builtin_bswap16/32/64), MSVC x64 supported since February 2025; language standard not documented
integration.platforms: any 32- or 64-bit MCU or host; SIMD on x86-64 (SSE2 intrinsics only), AArch64 NEON and ESP32-S3; unaligned-load fast paths on ESP32, Cortex-M4/M7, Teensy, x86-64 and AArch64; byte-wise fallbacks elsewhere
integration.thread_safety: not documented; from the code, all decode state (Huffman tables, quantisation tables, 2 KB file buffer, 2048-pixel buffer) lives inside each JPEGDEC object and the lookup tables are const, so separate objects should be independent, but one object must not be shared
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false - TJpgDec (and Bodmer's TJpg_Decoder wrapper's drawJpg plus tft_output(x, y, w, h, bitmap) callback) and picojpeg have different APIs; porting a draw callback to JPEGDEC's JPEGDRAW struct (x, y, iWidth, iHeight, pPixels, pUser) is a small change

gotchas: Open memory-safety bug (issue #119, April 2026, no maintainer reply): JPEGDecodeMCU_P computes &sMCUs[iMCU & 0xffffff], so when the decode loop passes MCU_SKIP (-8), as it does for the chroma blocks of a colour progressive JPEG decoded to 8-bit gray or dithered output (and, by the same code, for MCUs outside a crop area), the pointer lands about 32 MB past the 384-entry array and the DC store still happens; confirmed in the current jpeg.inl. The baseline path (JPEGDecodeMCU) checks iMCU < 0 and is not affected.

Harness flaw behind the 1.7x: Bodmer's TJpg_Decoder ships tjpgdcnf.h with JD_FASTDECODE 1 and JD_TBLCLIP 0, not TJpgDec's table-driven Huffman level 2 or table clipping. Espressif's esp_jpeg table (ESP32-S3, 320x180 image, RGB888) has TJpgDec at 62 ms in that configuration versus 46 ms with JD_TBLCLIP 1 and JD_FASTDECODE 2 (1.35x, derived from page data), so against a fully configured TJpgDec the lead would be nearer 1.3x (estimate, different image) at the old 32 ms figure. TJpgDec's decode-only callback also memcpys every block while JPEGDEC's returns at once, and its draw callback advances the DMA buffer index before pushing, so the decode+draw column displays the previous block (timing comparable, output wrong).

Each JPEGDEC object holds the whole JPEGIMAGE struct (about 17.9 KB), so keep it global, static or heap-allocated rather than on a small RTOS task stack; library.properties says 32K+ RAM MCUs, the README says 20K.

Building outside Arduino needs -D__LINUX__ (or __MACH__, ESP_PLATFORM, _WIN64, __MCUXPRESSO), otherwise the header pulls in Arduino.h; linux/makefile installs with sudo cp into /usr/local. Other open reports: baseline AC tables with codes over 10 bits that do not start with six 1 bits are rejected (the slow-table fallback is commented out), images that stopped loading after 1.6.1 on an STM32H743 (#123), and red/blue swapped for some images on the Apple M1 NEON path (#120).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick JPEGDEC for baseline JPEGs on a microcontroller streaming straight to a display with 20-32 KB of RAM to spare; pick lowzag when the files are progressive and must be shown scaled on an ESP32, and libjpeg-turbo (or jpeg-nitro for multi-threaded host decoding) on desktops, where JPEGDEC has no published comparison.
verified_claims_summary: atomic14's independent ESP32-S3 harness (PlatformIO espressif32 unpinned, Arduino framework, -Ofast) decoded one 280x240 baseline 4:2:0 JPEG (23,362 bytes, restart interval 18) from RAM to RGB565 once per library per pass, timed with millis(): JPEGDEC 32 ms against 55 ms for Bodmer's TJpg_Decoder (TJpgDec R0.03 at JD_FASTDECODE 1) and 108 ms for Bodmer's JPEGDecoder (picojpeg), 1.7x and 3.4x. A later SIMD build of JPEGDEC was recorded at 23 ms without re-running the other rows, and Espressif's ESP32_JPEG was fastest at 20 ms; the README's own chart gives only JPEGDEC's per-MCU timings.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-03-13, NLnet-funded, Apache-2.0, 631 stars) and easy to vendor as one translation unit, but the progressive-path out-of-bounds write (#119) is open and the 1.7x lead was measured against TJpgDec in a non-fastest build configuration, so treat it as an upper bound.
